title: Book One · Chapter 69: A Walk Without Hints
story:
Mei looks at the map and says the school is too small.

“The school is much bigger than Mr Qiu's stall.”

“The paper is not the whole street,” Ronan says.

“I know. But your stall is as big as the school.”

Leo puts his hand over the stall. “It has important pencils.”

Miss Wu lets them show their map in class. They have part of the last lesson for it. She checks other children's work at her desk. She tells the three to speak quietly.

Ronan wants praise for the arrows. Instead Mei looks at the roofs.

“I could draw a school sign,” Mei says. “Then people would know.”

“We wrote SCHOOL there.”

“Some people read slowly.”

Ronan thinks of his own reading sheet. He moves his hand away from the paper.

“Can you make it small?”

“Yes. I do not need your whole street.”

Mei draws a tiny book on the school roof. Beside the tea shop, she draws a cup. Mr Qiu's stall gets a pencil. The buildings stay the same size. The signs help Ronan tell them apart much faster.

Miss Wu comes to look.

“Who used this map?” she asks.

“My mum,” Ronan says.

“Your mum helped with the map. Did anyone else use it?”

They are quiet.

After school, Mei agrees to walk from the start to the tea shop. Mum will come too. Leo wants to come too. But his father is taking him to the station. He waves from the gate and goes the other way.

Ronan watches Leo leave. He wanted to walk with Leo too. Then Mei takes the map.

“No hints,” she says.

Mum nods. “I will only stop you if we need to stop for the road.”

Mei finds the first corner. She finds Mr Qiu's stall. Then she stops.

“There are two little paths here.”

“The right one,” Ronan says at once.

She looks at him.

He closes his mouth.

On the map, only one path is drawn. Mei touches the empty space for the other path. The second path leads to a yard, not East Court. It is narrow, but it is there.

Ronan draws it. Mum asks the woman at the yard about it. Then Ronan writes NO WAY THROUGH beside that path.

Now Mei reaches the tea shop without another hint. She stands under the three white stones.

“This part works,” she says.

Ronan wanted praise for the whole map. Now this part is clear. Her walk helped him check it.

Mum buys one cup of warm water at the tea shop. She asks for two empty cups too. They sit by the door. She divides the water between the three cups.

Mei puts the map on her knees. She does not draw anything else.

“Would you like to put your name on it?” Ronan asks.

“I did the signs. You and Leo did the roads.”

He writes all three names, with a small word beside each. Mei checks hers, then takes a long drink.

“Can you walk the whole map again on Sunday?” Ronan asks Mei. She shakes her head. She is going to draw with her cousin.

“We can use someone else,” she says.

“But you found the path.”

“And now it is on the map.”

He looks down. She is right. Mei cannot come on Sunday. But the path is on the map now. Someone else can use the map to find it.

When Leo sees the map next day, he points at the pencil sign.

“That is very like my pencil.”

“It is shorter,” Mei says.

Leo holds his pencil up. It is shorter too.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- hints＝提示
- tell them apart＝分清它们
- no way through＝此路不通
- divides＝分开、分配

额外情节词（不要求本章全部记住）：roof＝屋顶；cousin＝堂／表兄弟姐妹。

## 读句提示

**Did anyone else use it?**

还有其他人用过它吗？did放在主语anyone前；it指地图。

## 理解问题

1. Mei实际使用地图时发现了什么问题？
2. 为什么地图上最后出现了三个人的名字？
